policy_title: Increase use of independent healthcare capacity
stated: Reform UK will harness independent and not-for-profit health provision in the UK and overseas, and offer tax relief of 20% on all private healthcare and insurance, aiming to relieve pressure on the NHS and improve care for all.

source.quote: Use Independent Healthcare Capacity We will harness independent and not-for-profit health provision in the UK and overseas. Tax Relief of 20% on all Private Healthcare and Insurance This will improve care for all by relieving pressure on the NHS. Those who rely on the NHS will enjoy faster, better care. Independent healthcare capacity will grow rapidly, providing competition and reducing costs.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS pressure and care access by expanding independent/not-for-profit capacity and subsidising private healthcare via tax relief — real verdict on waiting times, capacity, and equity of access warranted.

A 20% tax relief on private healthcare spending and insurance premiums directly reduces the net cost for users, raising real money kept — a concrete, material improvement in take-home value for those who pay privately.

The tax relief forgoes identifiable revenue; if uptake is substantial (the stated aim), this widens the funding gap unless offset elsewhere, producing a specific fiscal sustainability concern routable to O12.

Tax relief on private healthcare disproportionately benefits higher-income households who can afford private care; a state subsidy flowing mainly to better-off users concretely widens the income/wealth gap, warranting an O14 verdict.

membership_note: Four fundamentals: O3 (core healthcare access and NHS capacity effects), O11 (direct tax-relief benefit to private-care users), O12 (revenue cost of the relief), and O14 (distributional skew of the subsidy toward higher-income households). No grounds for O10, O9, O6, or others.
